title: What does the main screen look like?
context: A small app with a messaging feel: you talk with the orchestrator, drop into any agent, see the decisions that need you, and can look at the board. House rules: no sideways scrolling, drawn icons only, no visibility toggles.

options.name: Threads, conversation, board on request
options.summary: Thread list on the left (orchestrator pinned first, then agents), the conversation in the middle with decision cards inline; the board opens in a side panel when you ask for it or click a card.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='10' y='15' width='300' height='150' rx='8' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.2' stroke='currentColor'/><rect x='20' y='25' width='70' height='130' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='55' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Threads</text><rect x='98' y='25' width='202' height='130' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='199' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Conversation</text><rect x='140' y='95' width='120' height='40' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='200' y='119' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Decision card</text></svg>
pros: Feels like a messaging app first
Board is one click away, not always taking space
cons: The board is out of sight until you ask

options.name: Three columns
options.summary: Threads, conversation and the board side by side at all times; at narrow widths the board moves under the conversation.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='10' y='15' width='300' height='150' rx='8' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.2' stroke='currentColor'/><rect x='20' y='25' width='65' height='130' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='52.5' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Threads</text><rect x='92' y='25' width='130' height='130' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='157' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Conversation</text><rect x='229' y='25' width='71' height='130' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='264.5' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Board</text></svg>
pros: Easy to see what a conversation changed

options.name: Board first, threads over it
options.summary: The board is home; clicking an entry or agent opens its conversation over it.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='10' y='15' width='300' height='150' rx='8' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.2' stroke='currentColor'/><rect x='20' y='25' width='280' height='130' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='160' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Board</text><rect x='150' y='45' width='140' height='100' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='220' y='99' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Conversation</text></svg>
pros: Puts the long-term memory at the centre
cons: Less like messaging, which is the point

recommendation: You asked for messaging first; decision cards inline bring the calls to you, and the board is one click away without crowding the conversation.
